title: How Satanism Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore Satanism, beginning with the origins of Satan in the Hebrew Bible and the emergence of dualism under Persian Zoroastrianism, then the New Testament Satan, and how early Christianity smeared rival gods (Baal Zebub, Lucifer, Baphomet) as demons. They trace how Milton and Dante shaped the modern devil and how the Enlightenment recast Satan as a metaphor for rebellion against authority. They cover how Christians accused heretics, witches and esoteric groups of Satanism without evidence, then discuss Anton LaVey and the Church of Satan (founded 1966, Satanic Bible 1969, borrowing from Ragnar Redbeard's Might is Right, the Eleven Satanic Rules of the Earth and Nine Satanic Sins), the Satanic Temple and its political stunts (Satanic Children's Activity Book, after school Satan club, invocations at city council meetings, Baphomet statue), and the Satanic Panic and cases of violence blamed on Satanism. The episode closes with a listener email about stuttering.
topics: Eleven Satanic Rules of the Earth
Satan in Paradise Lost and Divine Comedy

segments.title: Opening banter and disclaimer
segments.summary: Hosts warn listeners with strong religious beliefs, introduce the episode and guest producer Matt Frederick, and joke about Satanists being kind of libertarian or liberal hippies.

segments.title: Origin of Satan in the Hebrew Bible
segments.summary: Early Judaism had no Satan because God was seen as all things; dualism entered through Persian Zoroastrianism, and Satan's role as adversary, or legal figure, varies across translations.

segments.title: Satan in the New Testament and rival gods as demons
segments.summary: The New Testament presents Satan as a supernatural opponent of God who tempts Jesus and is linked to the serpent in Eden. Names like Beelzebub and Baal were corruptions of rival Canaanite and Phoenician gods, smeared by early Christians.

segments.title: Lucifer, Milton, Dante and the Enlightenment
segments.summary: The King James Bible rendered Lucifer as Satan's name though it was Latin for morning star. Milton and Dante shaped the fallen-angel image, and the Enlightenment recast Satan as a metaphor for free thought and rebellion against the establishment.

segments.title: Accusations of Satanism against heretics and witches
segments.summary: Anything opposing organized Christianity was labeled Satanic, leading to the persecution of mostly women accused of witchcraft, folk healers and midwives. Esoteric groups such as the Cathars, Knights Templar and Luciferians were labeled Satanist, though there is no evidence of an organized long-term Satan-worshipping group.

segments.title: Anton LaVey's background and the Church of Satan founding
segments.summary: Anton LaVey, born Howard Stanton Levey in Chicago, claimed a colorful past that researchers doubt. He hosted paranormal lectures in the 1960s, attracted Hollywood figures, founded the Church of Satan in 1966 and published the Satanic Bible in 1969.

segments.title: Might is Right influence, rituals and the Eleven Satanic Rules
segments.summary: LaVey's Satanic Bible is accused of borrowing from Ragnar Redbeard's Might is Right (1890). Rituals of compassion, lust and destruction are described as psychodrama. The hosts read the Eleven Satanic Rules of the Earth.
topics: Eleven Satanic Rules of the Earth

segments.title: Nine Satanic Sins, Church of Satan today and the Satanic Temple
segments.summary: The Nine Satanic Sins are listed, membership in the Church of Satan costs two hundred dollars and includes a card, and critics say the church declined after LaVey died under Peter Gilmore. The Satanic Temple is introduced as a politically active group with a Satanic Children's Activity Book.

segments.title: Satanic Temple political projects and the after school Satan club
segments.summary: The Satanic Temple uses Satanism as a poison pill in church-state debates: it answers Christian pamphlets in schools, delivers invocations at city council meetings, and proposes an after school Satan club countering the Good News Club.

segments.title: Violence blamed on Satanism and the Satanic Panic
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the Satanic Panic of the 1980s, heavy metal and Ozzy Osbourne imagery, and killers such as Richard Ramirez and David Berkowitz who claimed demonic motives. Satanists are described as atheists who do not harm children and do not worship a literal Satan.
topics: quote on love from Satanic Bible

segments.title: Listener mail on stuttering
segments.summary: Listener Richard Adrian Owitz writes about living with stuttering since age five and performing as a shanty singer at the San Francisco maritime park.
